metadata.description: A Unique name used for the Virtual Machine domain and also for generating resource names. Defaults to a value prefixed with "aiovm-".
Type of authentication to use on the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
SSH key or password for the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
The size of the VM, at least 16GB RAM is required

variables.$fxv#0:
#cloud-config

package_update: true
package_upgrade: true

apt:
  preserve_sources_list: true
  sources:
    msft.list:
      source: 'deb [signed-by=$KEY_FILE] https://packages.microsoft.com/ubuntu/24.04/prod noble main'
      keyid: BC528686B50D79E339D3721CEB3E94ADBE1229CF
    azurecli.list:
      source: 'deb [signed-by=$KEY_FILE] https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/azure-cli noble main'
      keyid: BC528686B50D79E339D3721CEB3E94ADBE1229CF
    kubernetes.list:
      source: 'deb [signed-by=$KEY_FILE] https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.32/deb/ /'
      keyid: DE15B14486CD377B9E876E1A234654DA9A296436

packages:
  - azure-cli
  - kubectl
  - git
  - moby-cli
  - moby-engine
  - wget  # Ensure wget is installed as it's used multiple times

write_files:
  - path: /etc/motd
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      ******************************************************
      * Provisioning Started - Please Wait          *
      * System configuration is underway            *
      ******************************************************

runcmd:
  # Single script block for robust error handling
  - |
    #!/bin/bash
    set -e # Exit immediately if a command exits with a non-zero status.

    # --- Error Handling Function ---
    handle_error() {
      local exit_code=$?
      local line_no=$1
      local command="${BASH_COMMAND}"
      echo "******************************************************" > /etc/motd
      echo "* PROVISIONING FAILED!                    *" >> /etc/motd
      echo "*----------------------------------------------------*" >> /etc/motd
      echo "* Error on or near line ${line_no}                   *" >> /etc/motd
      echo "* Exit Code: ${exit_code}                            *" >> /etc/motd
      # Optionally include the failed command if it's not too long/complex
      # echo "* Command: ${command}                               *" >> /etc/motd
      echo "* Please check cloud-init logs for details:        *" >> /etc/motd
      echo "* /var/log/cloud-init.log                        *" >> /etc/motd
      echo "* /var/log/cloud-init-output.log                 *" >> /etc/motd
      echo "******************************************************" >> /etc/motd
      exit $exit_code # Exit script with the same error code
    }

    # --- Trap ERR signal ---
    # Call handle_error function, passing the line number, when ERR signal is received
    trap 'handle_error $LINENO' ERR

    # --- Start Provisioning Steps ---

    # Set environment variables used in later steps.
    MYUSER=$(id -un 1000)
    MYHOME=$(eval echo ~$MYUSER)
    MYWORK="/workspaces" # Assuming this directory exists or is standard
    LOCATION={{{location}}}
    RESOURCE_GROUP={{{resource_group}}}
    RESOURCE_NAME={{{resource_name}}}

    # -------------------------
    # Step 1 of 8: Install prerequisites.
    # -------------------------
    echo "******************************************************" > /etc/motd
    echo "* Step 1 of 8: Installing prerequisites           *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "*----------------------------------------------------*" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* Installing required tools like docker, k3d, helm, *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* step CLI, az CLI, and necessary extensions.     *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "******************************************************" >> /etc/motd

    SYSTEM_NAME=$(uname -r)
    # Using moby-engine from packages, so manual docker install might not be needed unless specifically avoiding moby
    # if [[ "$SYSTEM_NAME" != *"microsoft"* && "$SYSTEM_NAME" != *"WSL"* ]]; then
    #   if ! which docker > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    #     echo "Installing docker.io..."
    #     # apt-get update already run by cloud-init package_update: true
    #     apt-get install -y docker.io
    #   fi
    # fi

    if ! which k3d > /dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "Installing k3d..."
      wget -q -O - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k3d-io/k3d/main/install.sh | bash
    fi

    if ! which helm > /dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "Installing helm..."
      curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/helm/helm/main/scripts/get-helm-3 | bash
    fi

    if ! which step > /dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "Installing step CLI..."
      # Consider checking architecture, but assuming amd64 for now
      STEP_VERSION="0.28.0" # Define version for easier updates
      STEP_DEB="step-cli_${STEP_VERSION}_amd64.deb"
      wget -q "https://github.com/smallstep/cli/releases/download/v${STEP_VERSION}/${STEP_DEB}" -P /tmp
      dpkg -i "/tmp/${STEP_DEB}"
      rm "/tmp/${STEP_DEB}" # Clean up
    fi

    # The azure-cli package should handle this, but keeping as a fallback/check
    if ! which az > /dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "Azure CLI not found via package manager, trying install script..."
      curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | bash
    fi
    # This might still be needed even if az cli is installed via package
    az aks install-cli --kubelogin-version 0.1.3 --aks-preview-cli-version 0.6.5 || echo "aks install-cli might have warnings/errors but continuing..."


    echo "Adding Azure CLI extensions..."
    az extension add --upgrade --name azure-iot-ops || echo "Failed to add azure-iot-ops extension, continuing..." # Allow failure? Decide based on requirements
    az extension add --upgrade --name connectedk8s || echo "Failed to add connectedk8s extension, continuing..." # Allow failure? Decide based on requirements

    if ! which k9s > /dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "Installing k9s..."
      # Fetch latest might be unstable, consider pinning a version
      K9S_DEB_URL=$(wget -qO- https://api.github.com/repos/derailed/k9s/releases/latest | grep 'browser_download_url.*linux_amd64.deb' | cut -d '"' -f 4)
      if [[ -n "$K9S_DEB_URL" ]]; then
        wget -q "$K9S_DEB_URL" -P /tmp
        dpkg -i /tmp/k9s_linux_amd64.deb
        rm /tmp/k9s_linux_amd64.deb # Clean up
      else
        echo "Could not determine k9s latest deb URL. Skipping k9s install."
      fi
    fi

    # -------------------------
    # Step 2 of 8: Create k3d cluster.
    # -------------------------
    echo "******************************************************" > /etc/motd
    echo "* Step 2 of 8: Creating k3d cluster               *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* (Setting forwarded ports and registry)          *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "******************************************************" >> /etc/motd

    echo "Creating k3d cluster (deleting if exists)..."
    k3d cluster delete || true # Allow failure if cluster doesn't exist
    k3d cluster create \
      -p '1883:1883@loadbalancer' \
      -p '8883:8883@loadbalancer' \
      -p '8884:8884@loadbalancer' \
      --registry-create k3d-registry.localhost:127.0.0.1:5000 \
      --wait
    echo "Setting kubectl context..."
    # Ensure .kube directory exists and has correct permissions if needed later
    mkdir -p $MYHOME/.kube
    chown $MYUSER:$MYUSER $MYHOME/.kube
    KUBECONFIG_PATH=$(k3d kubeconfig write k3s-default) # Get path to written config
    cp "$KUBECONFIG_PATH" "$MYHOME/.kube/config" # Copy to default user location
    chown $MYUSER:$MYUSER "$MYHOME/.kube/config"
    chmod 600 "$MYHOME/.kube/config"
    # Set context for root user running the script
    kubectl config use-context k3d-k3s-default
    kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=azure-iot-operations


    # -------------------------
    # Step 3 of 8: Arc-enable the Kubernetes cluster.
    # -------------------------
    echo "******************************************************" > /etc/motd
    echo "* Step 3 of 8: Arc-enabling Kubernetes cluster...   *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "******************************************************" >> /etc/motd

    echo "Logging into Azure using Managed Identity..."
    az login --identity
    echo "Connecting cluster to Azure Arc..."
    # Use the kubeconfig generated by k3d for the root user
    az connectedk8s connect --name "$RESOURCE_NAME" --location "$LOCATION" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --correlation-id "" # Pass empty correlation-id for automation

    # -------------------------
    # Step 4 of 8: Create Storage Account.
    # -------------------------
    # Derive a unique suffix from RESOURCE_NAME. Ensure lowercase and alphanumeric. Max length 24.
    UNIQUE_SUFFIX=$(echo "$RESOURCE_NAME" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -cd '[:alnum:]' | head -c 18)
    STORAGE_ACCOUNT="st${UNIQUE_SUFFIX}"
    STORAGE_ACCOUNT=$(echo "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" | head -c 24) # Enforce max length 24

    echo "******************************************************" > /etc/motd
    echo "* Step 4 of 8: Ensuring Storage Account exists      *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "*----------------------------------------------------*" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* Storage Account:                                  *" >> /etc/motd
    printf "* %-46s *\n" "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" >> /etc/motd
    echo "******************************************************" >> /etc/motd

    echo "Checking for storage account $STORAGE_ACCOUNT..."
    if az storage account show --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" &> /dev/null; then
      echo "Storage account $STORAGE_ACCOUNT already exists."
    else
      echo "Creating storage account $STORAGE_ACCOUNT..."
      az storage account create --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --location "$LOCATION" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --enable-hierarchical-namespace true --sku Standard_RAGRS --kind StorageV2 --output none
    fi

    echo "Getting Storage Account Resource ID..."
    SA_RESOURCE_ID=$(az storage account show --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv)
    if [[ -z "$SA_RESOURCE_ID" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: Failed to get Resource ID for Storage Account $STORAGE_ACCOUNT"
      exit 1 # Force failure
    fi

    # -------------------------
    # Step 5 of 8: Create Schema Registry.
    # -------------------------
    # Derive names, ensuring lowercase, alphanumeric, and reasonable length
    SR_UNIQUE_SUFFIX=$(echo "$RESOURCE_NAME" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -cd '[:alnum:]' | head -c 18)
    SCHEMA_REGISTRY="sr${SR_UNIQUE_SUFFIX}"
    SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE="srn${SR_UNIQUE_SUFFIX}"
    SCHEMA_REGISTRY=$(echo "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" | head -c 24) # Adjust length limits as needed
    SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE=$(echo "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE" | head -c 24) # Adjust length limits as needed

    echo "******************************************************" > /etc/motd
    echo "* Step 5 of 8: Ensuring Schema Registry exists      *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "*----------------------------------------------------*" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* Schema Registry:                                  *" >> /etc/motd
    printf "* %-46s *\n" "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* Registry Namespace:                              *" >> /etc/motd
    printf "* %-46s *\n" "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE" >> /etc/motd
    echo "******************************************************" >> /etc/motd

    echo "Checking for Schema Registry $SCHEMA_REGISTRY..."
    if az iot ops schema registry show --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" &> /dev/null; then
      echo "Schema registry $SCHEMA_REGISTRY already exists."
    else
      echo "Creating Schema Registry $SCHEMA_REGISTRY..."
      az iot ops schema registry create --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --registry-namespace "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE" --sa-resource-id "$SA_RESOURCE_ID" --output none
    fi

    # -------------------------
    # Step 6 of 8: Initialize IoT Operations.
    # -------------------------
    echo "******************************************************" > /etc/motd
    echo "* Step 6 of 8: IoT Ops Init                       *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* Command:                                          *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* az iot ops init --cluster \"$RESOURCE_NAME\"        *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* --resource-group \"$RESOURCE_GROUP\"    *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "******************************************************" >> /etc/motd

    echo "Checking if IoT Operations is initialized on cluster $RESOURCE_NAME..."
    # Need a reliable way to check init status, 'show' might require an instance name. Using a placeholder check.
    # This might need adjustment based on `az iot ops` behavior. Assume `init` is idempotent or check resources it creates.
    # For simplicity, we run init if a key resource (like 'aio-dp-reader-proxy') doesn't exist.
    if ! kubectl get deployment aio-dp-reader-proxy -n azure-iot-operations &> /dev/null; then
      echo "Initializing IoT Operations on cluster $RESOURCE_NAME..."
      # Pass --no-tls or configure TLS properly for k3d if needed
      az iot ops init --cluster "$RESOURCE_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --kv-id "" # Pass required --kv-id or --no-tls etc. Adapt as needed! Example: --no-tls
    else
      echo "IoT Operations appears to be already initialized on cluster $RESOURCE_NAME."
    fi

    # -------------------------
    # Step 7 of 8: Create IoT Ops Instance.
    # -------------------------
    echo "Getting Schema Registry Resource ID..."
    SR_RESOURCE_ID=$(az iot ops schema registry show --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv)
     if [[ -z "$SR_RESOURCE_ID" ]]; then
      echo "ERROR: Failed to get Resource ID for Schema Registry $SCHEMA_REGISTRY"
      exit 1 # Force failure
    fi
    INSTANCE_NAME="${RESOURCE_NAME}-instance"

    echo "******************************************************" > /etc/motd
    echo "* Step 7 of 8: Ensuring IoT Ops Instance exists     *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* Command: az iot ops create ...                  *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* Instance Name:                                    *" >> /etc/motd
    printf "* %-46s *\n" "$INSTANCE_NAME" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* (See logs for full command details)             *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "******************************************************" >> /etc/motd

    echo "Checking for IoT Ops instance $INSTANCE_NAME..."
    # Use 'az iot ops instance show' when available, or check for a deployed resource.
    # Using a placeholder check for a common deployment from the instance.
    if ! kubectl get deployment aio-mq-dmqtt-frontend -n azure-iot-operations &> /dev/null; then
        echo "Creating IoT Ops instance $INSTANCE_NAME..."
        az iot ops instance create \
            --cluster "$RESOURCE_NAME" \
            --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
            --name "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
            --sr-resource-id "$SR_RESOURCE_ID" \
            --broker-frontend-replicas 1 \
            --broker-frontend-workers 1 \
            --broker-backend-part 1 \
            --broker-backend-workers 1 \
            --broker-backend-rf 1 \
            --broker-mem-profile Low \
            --output none # Add --no-progress ?
    else
        echo "IoT Ops instance $INSTANCE_NAME appears to already exist."
    fi


    # -------------------------
    # Step 8 of 8: Configure kube config and Finalize.
    # -------------------------
    echo "******************************************************" > /etc/motd
    echo "* Step 8 of 8: Configuring kube config            *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* and Finalizing Provisioning                     *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "******************************************************" >> /etc/motd

    echo "Ensuring kubeconfig is in user's home directory..."
    # The config was already copied in Step 2, ensure permissions again just in case.
    install -D -o "$MYUSER" -g "$MYUSER" -m 600 "$KUBECONFIG_PATH" "$MYHOME/.kube/config"

    echo "Setting ownership for workspace directory..."
    # Ensure the target directory exists before changing ownership
    mkdir -p "$MYWORK"
    chown -R "$MYUSER":"$MYUSER" "$MYWORK"

    # -------------------------
    # Final Success Message
    # -------------------------
    # Disable the error trap before the final MOTD update
    trap - ERR

    echo "******************************************************" > /etc/motd
    echo "* PROVISIONING COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY!      *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "*----------------------------------------------------*" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* System is ready.                                *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* Kubeconfig set for user '$MYUSER'                 *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "* Run 'kubectl get pods -A' to check cluster.     *" >> /etc/motd
    echo "******************************************************" >> /etc/motd

    echo "Cloud-init script finished successfully."
